articles.title: EUA: jurado dissidente em julgamento de enfermeira quebra o silêncio | G1
articles.standfirst: Jurado pivô de impasse no julgamento anulado de Lindsay Clancy, que enforcou os 3 filhos, quebrou o silêncio nesta semana sobre o caso. Defesa alega psicose pós-parto, enquanto Promotoria buscava condenação por triplo homicídio.
articles.summary: Jurado pivô de impasse no julgamento anulado de Lindsay Clancy, que enforcou os 3 filhos, quebrou o silêncio nesta semana sobre o caso. Defesa alega psicose pós-parto, enquanto Promotoria buscava condenação por triplo homicídio.
articles.body:
Ao lado de seu advogado, Lindsay Clancy, acusada de homicídio por matar os três filhos, olha ao júri durante julgamento de seu caso, em 1º de setembro de 2026. — Foto: Greg Derr/ Pool via Reuters

O jurado que se tornou o pivô do anulamento do julgamento de Lindsay Clancy, enfermeira que matou os 3 filhos nos Estados Unidos , quebrou o silêncio nesta semana e falou sobre o caso com a mídia norte-americana.

Michael Desronvil afirmou, em declaração enviada ao site NewsNation, que "não tinha dúvidas" de que Clancy era culpada, porém ele indicou sentir que era boicotado por seus colegas durante as deliberações. Ele era o único dos 12 jurados que era a favor de condenar Clancy por triplo homicídio.

“Eu não tive dúvidas [da culpa de Clancy]. Enquanto tentava explicar diferentes teorias possíveis durante a deliberação, eu era constantemente interrompido, como se eu tivesse dúvidas diante das provas apresentadas. Considerando todas as provas físicas, as principais testemunhas e o que a promotoria apresentou, achei que havia provas suficientes de que ela sabia exatamente o que estava fazendo e que havia planejado [o crime]”, disse Desronvil em declaração fornecida ao NewsNation por meio de um porta-voz.

O julgamento de Lindsay Clancy, que matou seus três filhos pequenos por estrangulamento em sua casa em 2023 , foi anulado no início do mês após o júri não ter conseguido chegar à unanimidade para o veredito mesmo após dias de deliberações.

Desde o início, o julgamento de Clansy se tornou famoso nos EUA e impulsionou um debate no país a discussão sobre psicose e outros transtornos pós-parto, com grupos de mulheres se manifestando a favor da enfermeira e defendendo mais atenção à saúde mental das mulheres.

A defesa de Clancy não nega os assassinatos, porém argumenta que ela agiu sob efeito de psicose pós-parto. Já a Promotoria afirma que ela estava consciente de seus atos e busca condená-la por triplo homicídio.

Atualmente, a enfermeira segue presa aguardando uma solução criminal para seu caso, enquanto a Promotoria analisa se apresenta novamente a denúncia para a Justiça para um novo julgamento com um júri novo.

articles.title: Ruas e avenidas de Teresina são interditadas para obras de esgoto | G1
articles.standfirst: Interdições parciais ocorrem em quatro bairros da Zona Norte nesta sexta-feira (18), durante obras de expansão da rede de esgotamento sanitário.
articles.summary: Interdições parciais ocorrem em quatro bairros da Zona Norte nesta sexta-feira (18), durante obras de expansão da rede de esgotamento sanitário.
articles.body:
Ruas e avenidas de quatro bairros da Zona Norte de Teresina têm interdições parciais nesta sexta-feira (18) para obras de expansão da rede de esgotamento sanitário. Os bloqueios ocorrem nos bairros Mocambinho, Primavera, Buenos Aires e Água Mineral.

As intervenções tiveram início às 7h e estão programadas para seguirem até as 18h . Em alguns pontos, os serviços começaram às 7h30. A orientação é que motoristas e motociclistas redobrem a atenção, respeitem a sinalização e utilizem rotas alternativas.

Segundo informações da Águas de Teresina à reportagem, o trecho com maior impacto é a Avenida Marechal Castelo Branco, no bairro Primavera. O local será sinalizado durante a execução dos serviços.

As obras fazem parte do plano de expansão da infraestrutura de esgotamento sanitário da empresa na capital piauiense.

articles.title: FATO OU FAKE: Entrevistas com candidados ao governo de PE no NE1 | G1
articles.standfirst: João Campos (PSB) e Raquel Lyra (PSD) foram sabatinados nesta semana.
articles.summary: João Campos (PSB) e Raquel Lyra (PSD) foram sabatinados nesta semana.
articles.body:
João Campos (à esq.) e Raquel Lyra (à dir.) durante entrevista à TV Globo — Foto: Reprodução/TV Globo

Os candidatos ao governo de Pernambuco João Campos ( PSB ) e Raquel Lyra ( PSD ) foram entrevistados pelo NE1 nesta semana. Conduzidas pelos jornalistas Márcio Bonfim e Maristela Niz, as conversas sobre os principais temas do estado foram exibidas ao vivo no telejornal.

O público pôde acompanhar a transmissão pela TV Globo e pelo g1 , que depois disponibilizou a íntegra, assim como o Globoplay . Foram convidados os candidatos mais bem colocados na pesquisa Datafolha divulgada em 11 de setembro .

Segunda-feira (14) - João Campos (PSB) – leia mais sobre a sabatina e veja íntegra acima

Terça-feira (15) - Raquel Lyra (PSD) – leia mais sobre a sabatina e veja íntegra abaixo

A equipe do Fato ou Fake checou as principais declarações dos candidatos. Leia:

"O Mercado de São José é da mesma forma. Foi feito um dos maiores achados arqueológicos da história do Recife, no mercado. Então, claro, a gente tem que respeitar a regra, inclusive, de preservação do patrimônio."

As obras no Mercado de São José começaram em janeiro de 2024, com previsão conclusão para janeiro deste ano.

Inicialmente, custariam R$ 21,4 milhões. Desde então, receberam nove aditivos que, juntos, totalizam R$ 8,3 milhões.

Entretanto, em março, quatro ossadas humanas foram achadas durante as obras no local. Por causa disso, o Instituto do Patrimônio Histórico e Artístico Nacional (Iphan) foi acionado e recomendou uma pesquisa arqueológica.

Com isso, as obras ficaram temporariamente paralisadas para identificação dos enterramentos. Até 2025, mais de 30 esqueletos humanos haviam sido identificados. A hipótese dos pesquisadores é a de que o local já tenha sido um cemitério.

"O resultado do concurso foi exatamente o mesmo, e a pessoa que supostamente tinha sido prejudicada trabalha desde o primeiro dia. Foi uma disputa entre duas pessoas com deficiência: uma pessoa, com deficiência física; e outra pessoa, com deficiência intelectual."

O concurso para procurador da Prefeitura do Recife ocorreu em 2022, e o advogado Marko Venício dos Santos Batista foi o único candidato aprovado para a vaga reservada para pessoas com deficiência (PCD). O resultado foi homologado em junho de 2023, restando apenas a nomeação e posse do candidato – o que não aconteceu de imediato.

Em 2025, dois anos depois da homologação, Lucas Vieira Silva, um candidato que havia ficado na 63ª posição da ampla concorrência (ou seja, que não era para PCDs), entrou com recurso pedindo mudança no resultado.

Como justificativa, apresentou um laudo com diagnóstico de autismo, emitido apenas após a realização do concurso. Silva é filho de uma procuradora do Ministério Público de Contas de Pernambuco e de um juiz que havia arquivado uma operação que investigava desvios na prefeitura, durante a gestão de João Campos.

Mesmo com pareceres negativos de três procuradoras de carreira, que consideraram que a mudança no resultado violaria o edital, a alteração foi publicada numa edição extra do Diário Oficial do Município, no dia 20 de dezembro. Três dias mais tarde, o então prefeito João Campos assinou a nomeação de Silva como procurador, publicada também em Diário Oficial.

O caso ficou conhecido como "fura-fila", ganhou repercussão nacional e virou alvo de críticas da sociedade e de entidades como a Associação Nacional das Procuradoras e dos Procuradores Municipais (ANPM) e a Associação dos Procuradores do Município do Recife (APMR), que divulgaram notas se opondo à mudança no resultado do concurso.

Posteriormente, um vereador do Recife pediu o impeachment de João Campos alegando crime de responsabilidade e atos de improbidade administrativa. O processo foi posteriormente rejeitado pela Câmara Municipal, cuja maioria era formada pela base de governo do então prefeito.

Após a repercussão, João Campos anulou a nomeação do filho do juiz e, em 6 de janeiro de 2026, deu posse ao advogado Marko Venício dos Santos Batista que havia sido o único PCD aprovado.

Ou seja, Batista acabou sendo nomeado, como afirmou João Campos na entrevista desta segunda. Mas, entre a aprovação a sua nomeação efetiva ocorreu uma mudança no resultado, posteriormente revertida.

"Eu abri as delegacias [da Mulher 24 horas], mas não todas elas. Só tinha, em Pernambuco inteiro, a Delegacia [da Mulher] de Santo Amaro que funcionava 24 horas."

Até março de 2023, somente a Delegacia da Mulher de Santo Amaro, no Centro do Recife, funcionava 24 horas por dia.

Em decreto assinado por Raquel Lyra em março de 2023, mais cinco Delegacias da Mulher passaram a funcionar 24 horas: Jaboatão dos Guararapes, Petrolina, Caruaru, Paulista e Olinda.

Depois, a Delegacia da Mulher do Cabo de Santo Agostinho também se tornou 24 horas.

São, atualmente, sete unidades das 15 espalhadas pelo estado com funcionamento ininterrupto. Não houve, no entanto, construção de Delegacias da Mulher na gestão atual.

"Eu tinha o direito de poder fazer uma opção entre a remuneração de governadora e a remuneração de procuradora do estado. O fiz e recebo pela Procuradoria do Estado de Pernambuco, sem acumulação com o salário correspondente ao governo do estado."

O artigo 38 da Constituição restringe apenas a prefeitos e vereadores a escolha de remuneração entre a de cargo público efetivo e a de cargo eletivo apenas a prefeitos e vereadores. Ou seja, governadores estão fora dessa hipótese.

Nos primeiros dias de seu mandato como governadora, em 2023, Raquel Lyra enviou um projeto de lei estadual sobre esse tema à Assembleia Legislativa de Pernambuco (Alepe). A lei estadual 18.139/2023, aprovada em 18 de janeiro, determina que a ocupante do cargo de governadora de Pernambuco também pode fazer a opção entre a remuneração de cargo público e a de cargo eletivo, como alegou Raquel Lyra na entrevista desta terça.

Na década de 1990, Alagoas havia criado um dispositivo sobre o mesmo tema – a lei estadual 5.729/1995. Mas ela foi declarada inconstitucional em agosto de 2014 pelo Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF), no julgamento da Ação Direta de Inconstitucionalidade (ADI) nº 1.381/AL.

Na ADI, a Corte reafirmou que o direito de opção de remuneração (acumulação ou escolha de vencimentos ao assumir cargos públicos/eletivos) esbarram nos limites do artigo 38 e do artigo 22 da Constituição. Essas normas vedam que leis estaduais ampliem as hipóteses de escolha de salários para além do que a Constituição estipula, ou seja: restringindo a prefeitos e vereadores.

Ao Fato ou Fake , a professora de direito constitucional e vice-diretora da Faculdade de Direito do Recife da Universidade Federal de Pernambuco (UFPE), Antonella Galindo, disse que a ADI de 2014 continua válida e tem "efeito vinculante".

Ela explicou: "Qualquer lei que a contraria [ADI] tem que ser considerada inconstitucional. Então, se houver alguma Ação Direta de Inconstitucionalidade contra essa lei daqui de Pernambuco, muito provavelmente ela vai ser declarada inconstitucional. Nesse caso, o Supremo entende bem literalmente mesmo que seria uma regra aplicável somente a prefeitos e vereadores".

Participaram da checagem: Artur Ferraz, Luiza Mendonça, Pedro Alves, Rafael Souza e Roney Domingos .

articles.title: Incêndios em áreas de vegetação mobilizam equipes há cinco dias em cidade no Centro-Sul do Piauí | G1
articles.standfirst: Dois incêndios atingem áreas de vegetação em São João do Piauí desde o domingo (13), segundo a Secretaria Municipal de Meio Ambiente.
articles.summary: Dois incêndios atingem áreas de vegetação em São João do Piauí desde o domingo (13), segundo a Secretaria Municipal de Meio Ambiente.
articles.body:
Dois incêndios atingem áreas de vegetação em São João do Piauí desde o domingo (13), segundo a Secretaria Municipal de Meio Ambiente. O primeiro foco começou nas proximidades de comunidades rurais e mobilizou equipes de combate por cerca de quatro dias. Um segundo incêndio foi registrado na quinta-feira (17), segundo o secretário Vinicius Moura.

Ao g1 , Vinicius Moura informou que o primeiro incêndio teve início na região da Comunidade Jacaré e da Vila Betânia. Equipes da Secretaria Municipal de Meio Ambiente, do Corpo de Bombeiros Militar do Piauí (CBMEPI), da brigada local e moradores atuaram no combate às chamas.

Segundo o secretário, o fogo foi parcialmente controlado apenas na quinta-feira (17).

"Esse fogo começou no domingo. No mesmo dia uma equipe foi no local e começou a atuar, mas não tivemos sucesso e precisamos retornar no dia seguinte, já com ajuda de retroescavadeira, caminhão-pipa e também com ajuda dos moradores. O Corpo de Bombeiros nos ajudou por dois dias também", iniciou o secretário.

Vinicius Moura informou ainda que as equipes devem retornar à região para verificar se ainda há focos de incêndio em áreas mais altas da chapada. Segundo ele, cerca de 80% das chamas já foram extintas.

Equipes precisaram partir para outro incêndio

Vinicius Moura informou ainda que, enquanto as equipes combatiam o incêndio iniciado no domingo (13), um novo foco de fogo foi registrado na divisa entre São João do Piauí e Pedro Laurentino . As equipes foram acionadas para atuar também na nova ocorrência.

Segundo o secretário, as equipes conseguiram controlar parte das chamas nas proximidades das comunidades da região. O trabalho de combate foi retomado nesta sexta-feira (19).

"Começou outro incêndio florestal ali na região, na divisa de São João do Piauí com Pedro Laurentino. As equipes se deslocaram pra lá e começaram o combate. Nossas equipes irão retomar o combate hoje de manhã", completou o secretário.

articles.title: Vereador de Porto Alegre é preso em operação sobre desvio de emendas | G1
articles.standfirst: Além de parlamentar Giovane Byl (Podemos), ação do Ministério Público cumpriu outros três mandados de prisão preventiva e nove de busca e apreensão. Caso apura destino de verbas e segue sob sigilo.
articles.summary: Ação do Ministério Público cumpriu quatro mandados de prisão preventiva e nove de busca e apreensão em Porto Alegre e Imbé. Caso apura destino de verbas e segue sob sigilo.
articles.body:
Vereador de Porto Alegre Giovane Byl (Podemos) — Foto: Giulia Secco/CMPA

O vereador de Porto Alegre Giovane Byl (Podemos) foi preso preventivamente na manhã desta sexta-feira (18). Byl é também candidato a deputado estadual . A prisão faz parte de uma operação que investiga desvio de mais de R$ 2 milhões em recursos da área da saúde .

Além do parlamentar, foram expedidos outros três mandados de prisão preventiva. Os alvos são um assessor parlamentar , um advogado e um ex-dirigente de uma instituição investigada na ação, que não tiveram os nomes divulgados. Ao todo, nove mandados de busca e apreensão foram cumpridos nas cidades de Porto Alegre e Imbé .

O g1 busca a defesa de Giovane Byl. Até a última atualização da reportagem, ainda não havia manifestação oficial da defesa do parlamentar.

Em nota, o presidente da Câmara de Vereadores da Capital, Moisés Barboza, diz que o Legislativo "seguirá prestando toda a colaboração necessária às autoridades responsáveis pela investigação".

A investigação aponta que o grupo incluía dirigentes de uma organização da sociedade civil (OSC), entidade privada sem fins lucrativos que executava projetos financiados com recursos públicos.

Segundo o MPRS, a entidade investigada recebeu mais de R$ 1,9 milhão dos valores analisados. A lista geral de alvos da operação inclui o vereador, um servidor do Legislativo Municipal, um advogado e dirigentes da entidade.

Conforme o Ministério Público, os valores eram retirados das "contas vinculadas aos termos de fomento, transferida para contas de livre movimentação da própria organização e, posteriormente, distribuída entre investigados, empresas e outros envolvidos".

Giovane Byl é candidato a deputado estadual nas eleições deste ano.

A ação foi realizada pelo Ministério Público do Rio Grande do Sul (MPRS), por meio do Grupo de Atuação Especial de Combate ao Crime Organizado (Gaeco), com o apoio da Brigada Militar. A investigação segue sob sigilo.

Operação do Ministério Público ocoreu nesta sexta-feira (18) — Foto: MPRS

O que diz a Câmara de Vereadores de Porto Alegre

"A Câmara Municipal de Porto Alegre foi surpreendida pela operação deflagrada pelo Ministério Público na manhã desta sexta-feira (18), no âmbito de uma investigação que envolve um vereador e um servidor do Legislativo.

Desde o início da ação, acompanho os procedimentos realizados também nas dependências da Câmara e reafirmo o compromisso desta Casa com a transparência, a legalidade e o pleno respeito às instituições.

O Legislativo Municipal seguirá prestando toda a colaboração necessária às autoridades responsáveis pela investigação, disponibilizando informações e documentos sempre que formalmente solicitados.

Neste momento, é fundamental respeitar a independência dos órgãos de investigação, bem como o devido processo legal e o direito à ampla defesa, sem qualquer julgamento antecipado acerca dos fatos ou de eventuais responsabilidades.

A Câmara aguardará o desenvolvimento das apurações e os esclarecimentos das autoridades competentes, adotando, dentro de suas atribuições, as providências que se mostrarem necessárias.

Presidente da Câmara Municipal de Porto Alegre"

articles.title: Carro pega fogo às margens da BR-101 em Parnamirim | G1
articles.standfirst: Motorista percebeu fumaça, conseguiu estacionar o veículo em local seguro e saiu antes que as chamas se espalhassem; ninguém ficou ferido.
articles.summary: Carro pegou fogo às margens da BR-101, em Parnamirim. Motorista percebeu fumaça, estacionou o veículo e saiu antes das chamas.
articles.body:
Carro pega fogo às margens da BR-101 em Parnamirim — Foto: Divulgação / CBMRN

O Corpo de Bombeiros Militar do Rio Grande do Norte foi acionado na manhã desta sexta-feira (18) para combater um incêndio em um veículo às margens da BR-101, na altura do bairro Cajupiranga, em Parnamirim , na Grande Natal.

O veículo, uma Fiat Strada, começou a apresentar sinais de fumaça enquanto era conduzido pelo motorista. Ele conseguiu estacionar o automóvel em um local seguro antes que as chamas se propagassem.

Pouco depois, o veículo entrou em combustão. Uma equipe do quartel do Corpo de Bombeiros em Parnamirim foi deslocada até o local e realizou o combate ao fogo.

As chamas foram controladas antes que o incêndio se espalhasse para outras áreas.

Ninguém ficou ferido. O incêndio provocou apenas danos materiais no veículo. As circunstâncias e as causas do incêndio ainda serão investigadas.

articles.title: Mãe de Garotinho morre em Campos dos Goytacazes | G1
articles.standfirst: Candidato ao governo do RJ cancelou agenda de campanha em Duque de Caxias para acompanhar o velório e o enterro, segundo assessoria.
articles.summary: A agenda de Anthony Garotinho, candidato do Republicanos ao governo do estado do Rio de Janeiro, foi cancelada nesta sexta-feira (18) após a morte de sua mãe, Samira.
articles.body:
Garotinho promete dobrar efetivo da Defensoria Pública do RJ — Foto: Reprodução TV Globo

A mãe de Anthony Garotinho , candidato do Republicanos ao governo do RJ, morreu nesta sexta-feira (18). A agenda de campanha prevista foi cancelada.

A informação foi divulgada nas redes sociais oficiais do político pela equipe do candidato. A causa da morte não foi detalhada.

Segundo a assessoria de Garotinho, ex-governador do estado e candidato a um novo mandato, ele participaria de compromissos de campanha em Duque de Caxias, na Baixada Fluminense, mas não comparecerá.

Garotinho seguiria para Campos dos Goytacazes , onde acompanhará o velório e o sepultamento da mãe.

"Em virtude do falecimento durante o inicio dessa madrugada de sua mãe SAMIRA, a agenda que GAROTINHO cumpriria durante todo dia de hoje em DUQUE DE CAXIAS ESTÁ CANCELADA. O deslocamento até a cidade de Campos dos Goytacazes leva em torno de 3 horas e ele tera que sair cedo para o velório e a seguir o sepultamento".

articles.title: Neblina afeta voos no aeroporto de Porto Alegre | G1
articles.standfirst: Visibilidade prejudicada suspendeu temporariamente as decolagens. Chegadas previstas a partir das 7h não foram afetadas e painel da concessionária Fraport já indica regularização.
articles.summary: Visibilidade prejudicada suspendeu temporariamente as decolagens. Chegadas previstas a partir das 7h não foram afetadas e painel da concessionária Fraport já indica regularização
articles.body:
Um nevoeiro afetou a visibilidade e provocou o atraso de cerca de 10 voos no Aeroporto Salgado Filho , em Porto Alegre , na manhã desta sexta-feira (18). As decolagens chegaram a ser temporariamente suspensas devido à neblina , mas as aeronaves já conseguiram partir e a situação foi normalizada.

Segundo funcionários do aeroporto, o painel físico de voos do terminal apresentou lentidão para atualizar os status das viagens e continuou indicando atrasos mesmo após as decolagens. No entanto, o site da Fraport, concessionária que administra o aeroporto, já registrava a partida dos 10 voos.

As chegadas de aeronaves previstas a partir das 7h da manhã não foram afetadas pela condição climática. Com a regularização das operações, o fluxo de passageiros em busca de informações nos balcões das companhias aéreas, que havia registrado aumento, também diminuiu.

As próximas partidas devem ocorrer normalmente, desde que as condições de visibilidade não voltem a piorar.

Neblina atingiu o Aeroporto Salgado Filho, de Porto Alegre, na manhã desta sexta-feira (18) — Foto: Reprodução/RBS TV

articles.title: Rompimento de adutora em Piracicaba interdita Avenida Nove de Julho | G1
articles.standfirst: Vazamento ocorre na Avenida Nove de Julho na manhã desta sexta-feira (18). Equipes do Semae trabalham no local.
articles.summary: O rompimento de uma adutora na Avenida Nove de Julho causa bloqueios no trânsito e mobiliza equipes do Semae para reparos emergenciais em Piracicaba nesta sexta-feira.
articles.body:
Uma adutora se rompeu e provocou interdição na Avenida Nove de Julho na região do bairro Paulista em Piracicaba (SP) na manhã desta sexta-feira (18). Pelo menos, quatro bairros podem ter o abastecimento prejudicado. Veja locais, abaixo.

Há transtornos o trânsito no trecho, que está bloqueado para motoristas que seguem sentido Avenida Doutor Paulo de Moraes e Centro da cidade.

Adutora se rompe e interdita Avenida Nove de Julho em Piracicaba — Foto: Edijan Del Santo/EPTV

Em nota, enviada à EPTV , afiliada da Globo para Piracicaba e região, a prefeitura informou que os bairros que podem ter abastecimento prejudicado devido ao rompimento são:

Adutora se rompe e interdita avenida de Piracicaba — Foto: Edijan Del Santo/EPTV

As causas do incidente ainda são desconhecidas. Equipes do Serviço Municipal de Água e Esgoto (Semae) trabalham no local. Ainda não é possível prever completamente os impactos do rompimento da adutora.

A Previsão é que os reparos sejam concluídos até às 12h desta sexta-feira.

Adutora se rompe na Avenida Nove de Julho em Piracicaba — Foto: Edijan Del Santo/EPTV

Moradores de Piracicaba (SP) relataram problemas com falta de água nas residências nesta quarta-feira (16). O problema acontece após as fortes chuvas que atingiram a região na última semana .

Apesar das grandes quantidades de água acumulada, segundo o Serviço Municipal de Água e Esgoto (Semae), a falta de abastecimento nas casas é causada justamente pelos temporais.

Isso por causa de dois fatores principais. O primeiro foi o rompimento de uma rede de água de 300 milímetros ocorrido na madrugada do dia 16 de setembro , no Bairro Pompéia.

O segundo motivo foi o acúmulo de sujeira na Estação de Tratamento de Água (ETA) "Luiz de Queiroz", trazida pelo Rio Piracicaba justamente por causa das chuvas, que levam os resíduos para o corpo hídrico.

"Em função das chuvas, carriou muitos detritos, areia, galhos. Então, a gente teve que fazer uma paralisação momentânea para fazer a limpeza daquela captação, para depois voltar a produzir água de uma forma normal. Aquela unidade, a estação de tratamento Luiz de Queiroz, é para produzir 750 litros por segundo. Está produzindo 330", explica Ronald Pereira da Silva, presidente do Semae Piracicaba.

Segundo a companhia, os reparos na adutora e a limpeza da estação deve ser concluída até as 14h desta quarta. Após isso, o abastecimento deve retornar ao normal.

Rompimento de adutora e sujeira deixam bairros de Piracicaba sem água após fortes chuvas — Foto: Prefeitura de Piracicaba

Ainda segundo o Semae, os bairros das seguintes regiões de Piracicaba foram afetados:

Segundo Semae, falta de água é causada por rompimento de adutora e acumulo de sujeira no Rio Piracicaba — Foto: Prefeitura de Piracicaba

Apesar da resposta da empresa, o morador Jean Souza, do Bairro Pompeia, conta que esse problema já acontece há certo tempo na região.

"A gente está desde o dia 14 sem água. A água vem, volta, para. A síndica está tendo que comprar caminhão pipa para fazer o abastecimento das caixas d'água", conta.

Ele tem uma filha pequena e conta que precisou pedir ajuda da sogra, que mora em outro ponto da cidade, para conseguir água, o problema não se resolveu.

"Minha esposa teve que ir para a casa da mãe dela ontem. Teve que ir lá para tomar banho, fazer as coisas. Aí hoje cedo ela já ligou para mim e falou que lá também está sem abastecimento de água".

Cíntia Marques Correa mora em outro ponto da cidade, na região do Chapadão, e também relata falta de abastecimento pelo menos desde sábado (14).

"Um pouquinho de água que chega, a gente corre, dá uma lavadinha, enche os baldes e faz o que dá para fazer, porque não tem como fazer. A água da caixa já esgotou, já não sai mais."

De acordo com o presidente do Semae, a culpa da falta de água são das tubulações antigas da cidade e se comprometeu em trazer uma solução para os moradores.

"São redes velhas, antigas. A gente vai consertar essa adutora antiga, já estamos fazendo a nova. Em coisa de 5 meses, o Semae entrega uma nova adutora com mais qualidade para a população", prometeu.

articles.title: Operação contra o PCC apreende dólares e reais em endereço de Sorocaba | G1
articles.standfirst: Operação investiga a infiltração de facção no transporte público paulistano. Ex-vereador de São Paulo Milton Leite não foi localizado e é considerado foragido pela Justiça.
articles.summary: A Polícia Civil realiza, nesta quinta-feira (18), buscas em um endereço ligado ao ex-vereador de São Paulo Milton Leite (União Brasil), em Sorocaba (SP).
articles.body:
Operação investiga infiltração do PCC no transporte público de São Paulo; Milton Leite, ex-presidente da Câmara, tem prisão decretada — Foto: Jornal Nacional/ Reprodução

A Polícia Civil fez buscas em um endereço ligado ao ex-vereador de São Paulo Milton Leite ( União Brasil ), em Sorocaba (SP), nesta quinta-feira (18). O ex-vereador de São Paulo é alvo de uma operação do Grupo de Atuação Especial de Combate ao Crime Organizado (Gaeco) que investiga o envolvimento da facção criminosa Primeiro Comando da Capital (PCC) no transporte público da capital.

De acordo com as autoridades, a busca tinha como objetivo localizar e prender Milton Leite, porque a polícia e o MP suspeitavam que o ex-parlamentar pudesse estar escondido em um imóvel da cidade, no bairro Jardim Natália, mas ele não foi encontrado.

No local, os agentes apreenderam documentos e dinheiro em espécie com uma pessoa que não soube explicar a origem dos valores. Foram encontrados R$ 280 mil e US$ 80 mil, que equivale a R$ 410 mil.

Por esse motivo, Milton continuava entre os alvos da ordem de prisão que não haviam sido encontrados. No total, a Justiça decretou as prisões de 16 investigados, sendo que dez deles tinham sido presos e outros seis estavam foragidos até a última atualização desta reportagem.

A Justiça decretou 16 prisões na operação, que teve início nesta quinta-feira (18). Até a manhã desta sexta-feira, dez suspeitos haviam sido presos e seis continuavam foragidos, incluindo Milton Leite, que não foi encontrado durante cumprimento de mandado.

"Estou em viagem, não estou foragido, e vou me apresentar às autoridades em até 24 horas. Vou provar minha inocência em todas as acusações".

Deflagrada nesta quinta-feira (17), a Operação Vectura Corrupta mira a infiltração do PCC no poder público e no sistema de transporte coletivo.

A investigação aponta que decisões estratégicas relacionadas a empresas de transporte suspeitas de ligação com a facção dependeriam do conhecimento ou do aval político de Milton Leite.

De acordo com informações obtidas durante a diligência, Milton estava em casa até a tarde de quarta-feira (16). Uma funcionária relatou aos policiais que ele saiu à noite para um compromisso de campanha.

Buscas na casa de Milton Leite — Foto: TV Globo

Entre os dez presos estão Levi dos Santos Oliveira, ex-presidente da SPTrans, Danilo Marco Morgado Silva, candidato a deputado estadual e ex-candidato à Prefeitura de Praia Grande, e Paulo Sirqueira Korek Farias, presidente do Esporte Clube Água Santa conhecido como Paulo Camarão.

Segundo o delegado titular da Delegacia de Investigações Sobre Entorpecentes (Dise) de Mogi das Cruzes, Fabrizio Intelizano, será apurada a hipótese de vazamento da operação durante a investigação. Ele argumenta, no entando, que a maioria do alvos foi encontrada.

articles.title: Thames Water's £10bn rescue deal should be rejected - MPs
articles.summary: A report on the future of Thames Water, urging the government to take action, has been published.
articles.body:
A cross-party committee of MPs has urged the government to reject a £10bn takeover proposal from Thames Water's creditors.

The UK's biggest water company owes roughly £20bn and has been working with creditors and government officials.

A report by the Environment, Food and Rural Affairs (EFRA) Committee has now said the government should consider placing it into special administration, a form of temporary nationalisation.

A Thames Water spokesperson said it needed to be "recapitalised and put on a firm financial footing".

Fears that the firm, which serves 16 million customers, could collapse first emerged three years ago.

The committee said a takeover plan by a consortium of more than 100 of its creditors did not have "the interests of the public, the company or the environment at heart".

The plan was seen as the final realistic option to avoid a special administration regime, after a previous deal with a US private equity giant collapsed.

Creditors, who collectively own about £17bn of Thames Water's debt, were previously warned by former environment secretary Emma Reynolds their plan did not go far enough to protect customers or the environment.

The new report said Thames Water, alongside other "poor-performing" water companies, was in a "doom loop" of fines for poor performance leaving it with less money to invest in improvements.

It warned the company would "likely accrue" more than £900m in penalties over the next five years.

The committee said laws needed to change to allow the government to trigger a special administration on performance grounds alone.

It also warned the top priority for the bidders, called London & Valley Water, was to "extract immediate value from Thames Water, not steer it to long-term success".

Alistair Carmichael, chairman of the committee, said: "We believe Thames Water can be turned around, but not by giving the keys back to the people who have been joy riding in the family car.

"The government should reject offers from the company's creditors in return for relief from fines for pollution and poor service."

Carmichael said "liabilities that the government will face in the short-term" could be recouped by a future sale of Thames Water once its finances and performance are back on track.

He added: "The chaos of another Thames Water-style saga must not be repeated."

Listen to the latest news from Oxfordshire

A spokesman for London & Valley Water said: "This group of investors has never been in control of the company and has never received a dividend from Thames Water.

"They have stepped in to fund a significant revenue shortfall to ensure Thames Water's record capital investment programme can continue without disruption."

He added: "Our enhanced proposal will address all feedback from Ofwat and ministers and is the fastest route to fix Thames Water's complex problems."

A Thames Water spokesperson said: "Turning Thames Water around will take a decade and require significant and sustained investment, but we are already making progress and this is a different business from the one it was two years ago."

They added: "Anything that delays the recapitalisation risks slowing the turnaround, disrupting investment and increasing the cost of delivering the improvements our customers and the environment need."

articles.title: A 25-year-old was outbid by $60,000 for a 116-year-old cottage; her handwritten letter convinced the owner to reject higher developer bids and sell it to her
articles.summary: Rest of World News: In a property market where a higher offer can seem impossible to beat, Karli Bryant discovered that sometimes a house is worth more than its price tag.
articles.body: In a property market where a higher offer can seem impossible to beat, Karli Bryant discovered that sometimes a house is worth more than its price tag. The 25-year-old had little reason to believe she would win the century-old cottage she had fallen for in Malanda, Queensland. Another buyer was prepared to pay $60,000 more. But Bryant had something the other bidders did not, a personal connection to the home and a handwritten letter that gave the seller a reason to choose her. Scroll down to read the story of connection and faith.A cottage with a pastAccording to a news report by ABC Information and Services, the timber-clad home was built around 1910, when the railway first reached Malanda, and was among the town's original cottages for railway workers. For Bryant, the property felt familiar long before she became its owner. She grew up in Malanda and attended the school next door. Her grandmother had also taught at the local primary school, and Bryant was studying to become a teacher there herself. Buying a home had once seemed far beyond reach. She initially viewed the cottage almost on a whim, but quickly began imagining what it could become.The letter that changed the saleAccording to the news report, Bryant decided to write to the home's elderly owner, who lived in Western Australia. Rather than focusing solely on the property itself, she explained what owning the cottage would mean to her. She wrote about her family ties to Malanda, her childhood nearby and her hopes of eventually raising children in the town she had always considered home. The personal appeal made an impression. On the other hand, other prospective buyers had offered substantially more money, but some planned to demolish the cottage and replace it with duplexes or units. Bryant intended to restore the old house and preserve its character. That difference ultimately mattered more than the extra $60,000, explains the report.The work beginsTwo days after settlement, Bryant and her partner were already deep into the renovation. The couple has even sent the former owner another letter, this time accompanied by a photograph of themselves standing proudly beside the sold sign. Bryant's purchase comes at a time when entering the property market has become increasingly difficult for younger Australians. In regional Queensland, prices have also climbed sharply since the last census, making a first home increasingly difficult to secure. For Bryant, however, the Malanda cottage represents more than an achievement in a challenging market. It is a chance to restore a piece of her hometown's history and create a future inside a house that has already survived more than a century.Image Courtesy: ABC Information and ServicesCatch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Bail set for ICE officer accused of lying and assault in non-fatal shooting in Minneapolis
articles.summary: A federal immigration officer charged with shooting a Venezuelan man during the immigration crackdown that roiled Minneapolis early this year made a brief first appearance Thursday before a Minnesota judge.
articles.body: MINNEAPOLIS — A federal immigration officer charged with shooting a Venezuelan man during the immigration crackdown that roiled Minneapolis early this year made a brief first appearance Thursday before a Minnesota judge, following months of legal and political battles over whether he would be extradited from Texas to face state charges. Immigration and Customs Enforcement officer Christian Castro, handcuffed and dressed in an orange jumpsuit, stood quietly in a glass enclosure in a Minneapolis jail courtroom for the hearing. He faces a separate hearing Friday in federal court for charges that he lied to investigators about the January shooting. Judge Paul Scoggin set bail at $400,000, or $200,000 if Castro agreed to a series of conditions, including that he sign a waiver saying he wouldn’t fight extradition back to Minnesota if he leaves the state while out on bail. Castro, 52, signed the waiver during the hearing but was still listed as a county jail prisoner late Thursday afternoon. He was arrested Wednesday in downtown Minneapolis by officers with the Minnesota Bureau of Criminal Apprehension on state charges of assault and false reporting of a crime stemming from the shooting of Julio Cesar Sosa-Celis. Castro’s attorney, Daniel Gerdts, declined to comment after the hearing. Christian Castro’s arrest happened months after Minnesota charged him In both the federal and state cases against Castro, prosecutors say he shot 24-year-old Sosa-Celis in the leg while firing through the front door of a Minneapolis home. They say Castro later falsely reported that he had been attacked with a broom handle and a snow shovel before firing his gun. Minnesota prosecutors charged him in May but were thwarted in their efforts to bring him from his home state of Texas, where he had been arrested. In the end, Castro came to Minnesota on his own to face federal charges in an indictment announced early this month. “Castro invented a story to justify shooting through a front door into a house with multiple people in it,” Hennepin County Attorney Mary Moriarty, the prosecutor handling the state case, told reporters after Thursday’s hearing. “His appearance in a Hennepin County courtroom today is a critical step in our efforts to hold him accountable for that shooting.” Friday’s hearing, in U.S. District Court in St. Paul, involves the separate federal case in which he is charged with making false statements to investigators regarding the shooting. Castro’s defense attorneys in that case have said he plans to plead not guilty. It’s the first Justice Department prosecution of a federal officer for actions taken during this year’s massive Operation Metro Surge, which brought thousands of agents to the Twin Cities and led to sweeping protests, arrests and the fatal shootings of two U.S. citizens by federal officers. The Trump administration says only federal authorities have jurisdiction Minnesota authorities have battled President Donald Trump’s administration over who should handle any charges against Castro. The Department of Homeland Security has called Minnesota’s prosecution of Castro “unlawful and nothing more than a political stunt,” saying only federal authorities have jurisdiction. Authorities, including Minnesota’s Bureau of Criminal Apprehension, arrested Castro in Cameron County, Texas, on May 29, after a Minnesota judge issued a nationwide warrant. Under Texas law, Castro could be detained for 90 days, during which Minnesota sought his extradition. But Texas Republican Gov. Greg Abbott last month refused to sign an extradition warrant. Castro was then released in Texas and soon after was indicted on the federal charges. He then turned himself in to federal authorities and returned to Minnesota on his own.

articles.title: Nestle 'assessing options' after Putin places Russian assets under state control
articles.summary: Rest of World News: Russian president Vladimir Putin has placed the Russian assets of Swiss food giant Nestle and French supermarket group Auchan under temporary administ.
articles.body: Russian president Vladimir Putin has placed the Russian assets of Swiss food giant Nestle and French supermarket group Auchan under temporary administration, according to a presidential decree published on Thursday. Nestle has said that they are assessing the situation and their options.The assets have been transferred to the temporary management of Russian company L.E.V. Management. The decree also covers assets linked to FM Logistics and the Russian business of former Leroy Merlin, now operating as Lemana Pro.The move affects two Nestle entities, Nestle Russia and Nestle Kuban, with shares held by Nestle's Swiss and German subsidiaries brought under the temporary management arrangement. Auchan's Russian subsidiary has also been placed under the same management.Nestle said on Friday that it was assessing the situation and its options, with a particular focus on its employees. The company operates six production sites in Russia and continues to manufacture products including coffee, confectionery, baby food and pet food there.Nestle had scaled back its Russian operations after Moscow launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. It halted investment, stopped advertising and withdrew several brands, including KitKat and Nesquik, while continuing to produce essential food products.Auchan, meanwhile, retained its Russian business after the invasion and placed its subsidiary under local management in 2023.Moscow's growing control over Western assetsRussia has increasingly used temporary administration to take control of assets belonging to companies from countries it considers "unfriendly". A decree signed by Putin in 2023 gave Moscow the mechanism to place such assets under temporary management.The measure has previously been used against Western companies including French food group Danone and Danish brewer Carlsberg, whose Russian operations were subsequently sold.The latest move comes after reports that a Russian company, KS Logistika, had asked Putin to place Nestle's Russian assets under temporary administration. The request reportedly cited Nestle's decision not to expand production capacity in Russia and to halt exports from its Russian factories. Reuters said it could not independently verify the information.Nestle generated about 2% of its global sales in Russia before the war, while the company currently employs thousands of people there. The company said it is now evaluating its options following the Kremlin's decision.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: New human rights report blames police for recent massacre in Haiti
articles.summary: A human rights group in Haiti has revealed new details about one of the country’s biggest massacres in recent years and unveiled security holes as authorities struggle to contain violent gangs.
articles.body: SAN JUAN, Puerto Rico — A human rights group in Haiti has revealed new details about one of the country’s biggest massacres in recent years and unveiled security holes as authorities struggle to contain violent gangs. The National Human Rights Defense Network said its report is backed by interviews with judges, police officials, armed civilians, the former head of a police station and more than 100 victims and their relatives. The report provides the most complete account of the attacks that gangs recently launched on the once peaceful farming community of Kenscoff near Port-au-Prince, with at least 164 people killed, more than 70 kidnapped and dozens missing. Strengthening security could have limited killings The human rights group asserted in its report released Wednesday that a “timely strengthening” of security could have prevented or limited the killings. “This lack of response is all the more concerning given that available information indicated the existence of a serious and imminent threat to the population,” it said. A spokesperson for Haiti’s National Police did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The human rights group noted that Kenscoff remained vulnerable after a January 2025 attack left at least 139 people dead or missing: “Serious institutional failures that contributed to the perpetration of this massacre had been highlighted. Unsurprisingly, security was never truly restored in the town.” It asserted that soldiers and special police units assigned to Kenscoff after the 2025 attack were later recalled “for reasons that remain completely unknown.” Security personnel had been cut Overall, security in the area was reduced by 60%, according to the report. Gangs attacked Kenscoff again in July, pulling back only to launch an even bigger attack in late August. A week before the massacre began, an armored vehicle was moved given a lack of personnel, “leaving a new opening for armed terrorist bandits and further weakening the city,” the report found. Requests from the former head of the Kenscoff police station for two additional armored trucks were ignored prior to the attack, it added. Days before the massacre, the group said that “armed terrorists” used surveillance drones to track movements and positions of law enforcement. They deployed scouts to the area, then infiltrated it and began monitoring roads, “identifying individuals likely to pose a threat to them.” The human rights group said government officials told them they did not hear plans about the attack but did notice drones flying over the city hours before it began. Tree trunks used to block roads Another warning sign: tree trunks were used to block roads hours before the massacre. One of the first victims was a 21-year-old man ordered to carry stones to block a road before he was shot in the head, the report stated. Among those killed were nearly two dozen people ages 65 to 90; 36 women; and seven children, including a 4-year-old. Victims included farmers, two pastors and a school principal who was beheaded. One man who worked at the Kenscoff police station had his eyes gouged and arms torn off, the report found. Gang members killed people sheltered at a school and a church, using bodies as barricades as police and civilians battled them for several hours. The report stated that armed men staged several attacks before entering Kenscoff to lure away police and weaken their defenses. The human rights group identified the victims and the way they died as it called on the government to provide financial, medical and psychological aid to survivors and their families. Report criticizes police passivity Between January and August this year, security operations had managed to reduce violence in Kenscoff by 66% prior to the attack, according to the nonprofit Armed Conflict Location & Event Data. But the report criticized what it called police passivity and the “disdainful disinterest” of high-ranking police officers to protect Kenscoff. It also questioned why a new U.N.-backed gang suppression force “remains barely perceptible on the ground, and its contribution to security operations remains difficult to identify.” A spokesperson for the force did not immediately respond to a request for comment on Thursday evening. The force said in late August that it was relieving Haitian police in certain areas to free up units so they could strengthen security in Kenscoff. The human rights group noted that another armed attack was launched within Kenscoff in mid-September. Kenscoff’s mayor issued a statement on Tuesday warning that drones continue to fly over his community and that disturbing videos and messages are being posted online as threats. “The convergence of these various signals must not be trivialized or ignored under any circumstances,” he wrote. “After more than 20 months of suffering, displacement, loss of life, and trauma caused by armed gang violence, the people of Kenscoff cannot be subjected to further tragedies that could have been prevented.”

articles.title: A San Diego military base has brought in almost 500 goats to eat dry brush, testing a wildfire-risk reduction idea its fire chief backed for years
articles.summary: US News: At Marine Corps Air Station Miramar in San Diego, a new group of workers has arrived with a rather unusual job description. They are expected to spend.
articles.body: At Marine Corps Air Station Miramar in San Diego, a new group of workers has arrived with a rather unusual job description. They are expected to spend the coming months eating their way through dry vegetation.The base has brought in 471 goats as part of a pilot project aimed at reducing the amount of flammable brush around parts of the installation. Rather than relying entirely on machinery or sending crews into difficult terrain, officials are testing whether controlled grazing can provide another way to prepare potential fire breaks.The trial began in September and is expected to continue until the end of the year, with the animals working across several hundred acres.Why goats are being used at MCAS MiramarThe project is focused initially on East Miramar, including land associated with the base's explosive ordnance division. The area presents a particular challenge because vegetation can become a source of wildfire fuel while the rough ground makes access difficult for personnel.For firefighters and other crews, reaching some sections on foot can be hazardous. That is where the goats come in. They can move across uneven ground while feeding on vegetation, with their grazing and trampling expected to reduce the amount of dry material left standing.As reported by NBC 7 San Diego, Cole Bush, who runs Shepherdess Land and Livestock with her mother, is overseeing the livestock operation. The company is supplying not only the goats but also the herding dogs, a shepherd and the other services needed to manage the herd during the trial. The animals did not need much encouragement when they arrived. They began feeding on a designated hillside within minutes.471 goats could clear up to five acres of vegetation each dayThe pace of the grazing will depend on the vegetation and conditions at each site. Bush said the goats can work through between one and five acres in a day. That means the 471 animals will have several months to work across the areas selected for the pilot. The intention is not simply to remove every plant. Instead, the grazing is being tested as a practical way of reducing vegetation in places where creating and maintaining fire breaks can be complicated.If the approach proves useful, the programme could eventually extend to other parts of the installation. One longer-term possibility is grazing along the base perimeter, where a reduced layer of vegetation could form a buffer between the military property and surrounding communities.MCAS Miramar tests goats as an alternative to machinery near sensitive habitatWildfire does not stop at the edge of a military installation, and fire moving through the region can affect land on either side of the base boundary. MCAS Miramar officials therefore see vegetation management as part of protecting both the installation and neighbouring communities.The goat project also gives the base an alternative to using heavy machinery in some locations.MCAS Miramar is home to several endangered species, according to officials. Bringing large machines into sensitive areas can disturb vegetation and habitat, while repeated vehicle movement can create its own environmental impacts. The pilot is intended to establish whether grazing can reduce some of those effects while still achieving the vegetation clearance required for fire management.The idea has been under discussion for yearsFor MCAS Miramar Fire Department Fire Chief Joshua Allen, the arrival of the goats follows a proposal that had been discussed for much of the past decade. Allen said he had supported the idea of using goats on the base for years. The current programme gives officials a chance to test the concept in actual working conditions rather than relying on assumptions about how well it might perform. It is also being described by the base as the first programme of its kind at a US military installation.The results will help determine what happens next. Officials will be able to assess how much vegetation the herd can manage, where grazing works most effectively and whether the approach can be incorporated into future wildfire preparation.What happens after the pilotReportedly, the goats are scheduled to remain on the base through the end of 2026. During that period, their work will provide a practical test of whether livestock can become part of the installation's longer-term vegetation management strategy.There are limits to what the trial can establish. Grazing is not being presented as a replacement for every form of vegetation clearance or wildfire preparation. Instead, the base is examining where the animals can do work that might otherwise require machinery or personnel in difficult terrain.If the results support wider use, the method could become part of how MCAS Miramar manages vegetation around its perimeter and other fire-prone areas. The same trial could also offer information for other military installations considering whether managed grazing is suitable for their own landscapes.The wildfire strategy behind Miramar's goats has decades of historyUsing goats to manage vegetation is far older than the Miramar experiment. Across Mediterranean landscapes, goats have shaped vegetation through centuries of pastoral grazing, with evidence from Crete showing sheep and goat pastoralism spanning roughly 2,000 years, as reported in the study published in Plos One, titled ‘2000 Years of Grazing History and the Making of the Cretan Mountain Landscape, Greece’. Their use for wildfire fuel reduction is more recent but also documented.California also has a documented history of using goats for fuel management. A 1982 US Forest Service report examined goats as a way to control brush regrowth on fuelbreaks, particularly in rough and mountainous terrain.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: After Japan’s 2011 disaster left pets behind, rescued Fukushima dogs were less attached and trainable, and carried 5–10 times more stress hormone
articles.summary: Rest of World News: A study finds that dogs rescued from Fukushima after the 2011 disaster show persistent high stress levels and lower behavioral attachment compared to other abandoned dogs. Their elevated cortisol levels highlight the lasting impacts of trauma on animals abandoned during crises.
articles.body: Seventeen dogs that were rescued after being abandoned in Fukushima following Japan’s 2011 earthquake and nuclear accident had lower trainability and attachment scores than a comparison group of abandoned dogs from Kanagawa, while their urine cortisol levels were five to 10 times higher. The findings came from a 2012 study published in Scientific Reports, which examined the animals during rehabilitation and found that the elevated cortisol levels persisted for as long as 10 weeks. The disaster forced residents within the Fukushima evacuation zone to leave their homes, and many pets were left behind. Researchers from Azabu University later received stray and abandoned dogs from rescue centers in Fukushima and compared them with abandoned dogs from Kanagawa that had not experienced the disaster. The study involved 17 Fukushima dogs and eight Kanagawa dogs, and all were given health care, exercise and time with people before undergoing behavioral assessment.The researchers used the Canine Behavioral Assessment and Research Questionnaire, or C-BARQ, to examine traits including aggression, separation anxiety, trainability, and attachment. They also collected urine samples to measure cortisol, a hormone associated with the body's stress response. The Fukushima dogs had significantly lower scores for aggression toward unfamiliar people, trainability, and attachment than the Kanagawa group, one month after arriving at the rehabilitation facility. Three months after arrival, the Fukushima dogs still had significantly lower attachment scores.Cortisol stayed elevated after the dogs were rescuedUrine cortisol levels in the Fukushima dogs were five to 10 times those of the Kanagawa dogs, and the difference remained after 10 weeks. The highest cortisol readings among the Fukushima dogs occurred during their first week at the rehabilitation facility. Levels declined significantly after the eighth day, but they remained substantially higher than those recorded in the comparison group. The researchers said the persistence of the difference made it unlikely that the findings could be explained simply by the normal stress of entering a new shelter environment.The dogs’ aggression toward unfamiliar people was lower during the first month than that of the comparison dogs, and the researchers said that the combination of high cortisol and lower aggression suggested that the animals' stress did not necessarily appear as obvious aggressive behavior. The study also found that the Fukushima dogs had lower attachment to their caretakers, and that difference remained statistically significant at the three-month assessment, despite the dogs receiving regular care and socialization.The sample was small, and the Fukushima dogs were older on average than the Kanagawa dogs. The analysis did not find an age effect that explained the behavioral differences, but the authors acknowledged that other factors that were associated with the disaster experience could not be completely eliminated.The rescue operation continued for yearsA separate 2018 epidemiological study examined 529 dogs admitted to two Fukushima shelters following the 2011 disaster, and found that the animals initially faced poor housing and husbandry conditions, unfamiliar or untrained staff, and insufficient exercise. Of the 529 dogs, 179 had detailed medical records, while 26% had verified ownership and almost 16% were eventually reclaimed by their owners. The same study found that 66% of the dogs developed diarrhea while at the shelters, with 17 different antibiotics used in treatment. Researchers found that using three or more antibiotics was associated with prolonged diarrhea symptoms, and also found that dogs with verified owners took longer to be adopted than dogs without verified ownership.The wider rescue operation therefore involved more than removing animals from the restricted area, since dogs had to be housed, medically treated, socialized and eventually placed with owners or adopters. The first response shelter operated under difficult conditions, and a second shelter was later established in Miharu with better housing and trained staff.The original cortisol study’s conclusion was that the Fukushima dogs showed behavioral differences and prolonged physiological stress after the disaster experience, and the authors said the findings were consistent with the animals having experienced an unusually severe crisis. The dogs were individually re-socialized after their health was assessed and were eventually placed with new owners, but their cortisol levels remained markedly higher than those of the comparison dogs during the 10-week observation period.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Texas parents sue daycare for $1 million after teacher encouraged son to fight another child in ‘fight club’
articles.summary: US News: Parents in Fort Worth, Texas, have filed a lawsuit seeking more than $1 million from a daycare after surveillance footage allegedly showed a substitut.
articles.body: Parents in Fort Worth, Texas, have filed a lawsuit seeking more than $1 million from a daycare after surveillance footage allegedly showed a substitute teacher encouraging her son to fight another four-year-old child. The incident reportedly occurred on April 27, 2026, at Arka Montessori Academy of Risinger. According to the lawsuit, the teacher allegedly grabbed, shook and dragged the child during the confrontation. The family claims their son suffered physical injuries and emotional distress. The case has also raised concerns about childcare supervision after state regulators reportedly cited the facility for safety and discipline violations. The allegations remain part of an ongoing civil case and have not been finally established by a court.Texas daycare faces ‘fight club’ allegationsThe parents, Heather and Richard Harris, filed the lawsuit on September 4, 2026, against Arka Risinger Educators LLC, the operator of Arka Montessori Academy of Risinger. Their son, identified as U.H. in court documents, was four years old when the alleged incident took place. The lawsuit claims that he was in a combined afternoon classroom after his regular teacher left. According to the complaint, another four-year-old initially struck U.H. before substitute teacher Chynia Johnson entered the classroom. Johnson's son was reportedly involved in the confrontation. The family’s attorney referred to the alleged conduct as a “child fight club”, a description that appears in the context of the lawsuit.Surveillance footage allegedly shows teacher’s actionsThe lawsuit claims that Johnson encouraged her son to continue fighting U.H. and physically handled the other child. According to the complaint, Johnson allegedly grabbed and shook U.H., shouted in his face and pushed him. She is also accused of pulling him towards her son while encouraging the children to continue fighting. The lawsuit further alleges that Johnson grabbed U.H.’s arm and leg, causing him to lose his balance and fall onto the classroom’s hardwood floor. The complaint claims that regular teacher Jacqueline De Luna was present but failed to intervene adequately.Mother questioned daycare’s explanationThe lawsuit states that Heather Harris became concerned when she arrived to collect her son and found him crying uncontrollably. According to the family’s account, staff initially described the incident as a fight between two children. Harris reportedly asked to view the surveillance footage after becoming dissatisfied with the explanation. The family claims that the footage showed Johnson’s involvement went beyond separating the children.Child reportedly suffered physical and emotional distressThe lawsuit alleges that U.H. suffered bruises and scratches on his arms, as well as headaches following the incident. His parents also claim that he experienced emotional distress and anxiety. According to the complaint, the child struggled with returning to daycare and had difficulty adjusting to another childcare environment. The family is seeking compensation for the physical and psychological injuries described in the lawsuit. The extent of the injuries and any long-term effects would be addressed through the legal proceedings.Texas regulators cited daycare for violationsThe Texas Health and Human Services Commission’s Child-Care Licensing Division reportedly investigated the incident and cited the daycare for multiple violations.The allegations and regulatory findings included concerns involving:Improper methods of discipline.Physical handling of a child.Yelling and humiliating treatment.Staff supervision and professional judgement.The lawsuit also refers to earlier safety and supervision concerns involving the facility. Regulatory citations and the parents’ allegations are separate from a final court determination of liability.What happened to the teacher?Reports stated that the caregiver involved was no longer employed by the daycare.At the time of the reported coverage, no criminal charges had been reported in connection with the incident. The civil lawsuit seeks financial compensation and alleges negligence and gross negligence.Parents seek more than $1 million in damagesThe Harris family is seeking more than $1 million in damages, along with exemplary damages, according to the lawsuit. The complaint alleges negligence, gross negligence and premises liability against the daycare operator. The requested amount is not an award already granted by a court. The case remains ongoing, and the allegations against the teacher and daycare operator have not been conclusively established through a trial or final judgment.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: America runs on data. If we don’t build the infrastructure, China will
articles.summary: Permitting delays, grid bottlenecks and supply chain constraints threaten U.S. AI leadership as competitors aggressively expand critical infrastructure.
articles.body: Most Americans don't think much about digital infrastructure because, for the most part, it is always there. We carry supercomputers in our pockets and expect instant access to our bank accounts, medical records, airline schedules, businesses, families and virtually any piece of information we need. We have become so accustomed to that availability that it is easy to forget there is an enormous physical infrastructure behind it. Both of us learned the value of information long before we entered the critical infrastructure industry. Kirk learned it beneath the ocean aboard U.S. Navy nuclear submarines, while Mike experienced it years later on the battlefields of the Global War on Terror with special operations forces. The missions and eras were different, but the lesson was the same: Having the right information at the right time can save lives. Knowing where your people are, understanding what is happening around you and acting on reliable information faster than an adversary can determine the outcome of a mission. That lesson applies to the challenge America faces today. The race for artificial intelligence isn't simply about who develops the best software or algorithm. It is also about who can build the power generation, transmission, data centers and workforce required to run it. If we fail at that part of the equation, it won't matter how innovative we are. 8 EVERYDAY THINGS THAT WOULD QUIT WORKING WITHOUT DATA CENTERS America has to build again For generations, one of America's greatest strengths was our ability to turn innovation into physical capability. We built interstate highways, ports, power plants, factories and telecommunications networks that fueled economic growth while strengthening our national security. THE MACHINES THAT KEEP AMERICA ALIVE ARE FAILING. WE FORGOT HOW TO REPLACE THEM We are at another such moment, except we aren't moving fast enough. Permitting delays, grid bottlenecks and supply-chain constraints are slowing new generation and transmission at precisely the moment AI and advanced computing are creating enormous new demand for electricity. China understands this. It is aggressively expanding power generation, transmission, manufacturing and computing capacity because technological leadership ultimately requires physical capacity. While Washington debates how AI should be governed, our competitors are making sure they have the infrastructure to deploy it. US ADVERSARY TURNS UP THE HEAT ON AMERICA’S AI LEAD WITH AN UNDERESTIMATED EDGE That is why the way we talk about data centers also needs to change. They aren't simply large commercial buildings filled with servers. They are part of what we call the Fifth Utility, the interconnected compute, power, fiber and digital infrastructure that supports banking, healthcare, transportation, commerce, emergency communications, national intelligence and defense. None of that means communities should accept development without asking tough questions. Residents deserve to know how projects will affect power, water, land, electricity rates and local infrastructure. Developers have an obligation to show up early, answer those questions honestly and invest responsibly in the communities where they build. DATA CENTERS FORGOT THE CONSUMER — AND THAT COULD COST AMERICA THE AI RACE We can protect communities and ratepayers while still building the infrastructure America needs. In fact, we must do both. The same is true of our workforce. Data centers and power plants don't build themselves. America needs electricians, line workers, welders, high-voltage technicians, construction professionals and mission-critical operators. Meanwhile, roughly 200,000 men and women leave military service every year with many of the qualities this industry desperately needs: technical discipline, leadership, adaptability and the ability to perform when failure isn't an option. FROM NEW YORK TO TEXAS, STATES SHOULD RESPECT LOCAL CONTROL ON DATA CENTERS Creating stronger pathways from military service into critical infrastructure careers should be part of our national strategy, not simply a workforce initiative. We spent our military careers understanding that information superiority matters only if you have the people, systems and infrastructure to deliver it when it counts. Technology may have changed, but the principle hasn't. We can protect communities and ratepayers while still building the infrastructure America needs. In fact, we must do both. America still has the capital, energy resources, technology and talent to lead the digital age. What we cannot assume is that those advantages will last while we take years to build what our competitors are building now. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP If America intends to lead the digital age, we need to start building like it. Kirk Offel is a Navy nuclear attack submarine veteran and the CEO of Overwatch Mission Critical, a Texas-based Service-Disabled Veteran Owned data center company that trains and hires future leaders for high-skill jobs in the data center industry. articles.title: By 2025, Arizona partners had turned 560 donated Christmas trees into Lake Havasu fish habitat, up from 68 trees just 3 years earlier and kept them from landfill
articles.summary: US News: Discover how Arizona's innovative Lake Havasu Fisheries Improvement Program has repurposed Christmas trees into vital underwater habitats, boosting fish populations while reducing landfill waste.
articles.body: Discarded evergreens are being bundled with other vegetation and placed underwater as fish habitat in Arizona. The Bureau of Land Management said the Lake Havasu Fisheries Improvement Program received 560 Christmas trees in the year before its December 2025 report, compared with 68 trees three years earlier. The program uses the donated trees and brush to add structure to parts of the lake that provide very little cover for fish.The program operates around Lake Havasu City, where the Bureau of Land Management manages Partners Point and works with local and state partners. The BLM says that brush trimmings are collected throughout the year, while fresh-cut Christmas trees are gathered after the holidays. Unsold trees from local retailers and donations from residents are also incorporated into the program, after which, the trees are bundled and transported by boat to predetermined locations in the lake instead of remaining above ground as waste.What happens after the trees go underwaterThe trees become part of a small underwater food chain, and according to the BLM, the brush bundles and pine needles gradually decompose. Insects, snails, mussels, crayfish and plankton feed on the decomposing material, while fish feed on those smaller organisms. The branches also provide places where smaller fish can hide from predators after the needles and leaves have fallen.The BLM says parts of the lake were relatively flat and lacked submerged habitat, with rocky and sandy areas but very little cover or food source for fish, and the addition of brush and Christmas trees provides both structure and organic material. The agency says that submerged bundles can supplement habitat for as long as 10 years.Arizona Game and Fish says its Aquatic Habitat Program conducts habitat surveys, and designs projects to improve reservoir fish habitat, and its work includes structures made from several materials, including PVC, wood and Christmas trees. The department lists Lake Havasu among Arizona reservoirs with designated fish-habitat locations.The locations are mapped because the underwater structures are intended to concentrate fish. Arizona Game and Fish provides GPS-enabled habitat files that anglers can use with compatible fish-finding equipment, and says that these structures are installed to help anglers locate fish throughout the year.A local recycling program that became a fisheries projectThe BLM says that the partnership began scaling up the idea in the early 1990s, and was building on earlier efforts by individuals who used discarded trees to improve fishing habitat in small private ponds. The Lake Havasu program eventually developed into a partnership that involved federal agencies, state agencies, conservation groups, anglers and volunteers. A separate BLM account published in November 2025 described the program as having three decades of stewardship and identified partners including the Bureau of Reclamation, U.S. Geological Survey, U.S. Fish and Wildlife Service, Arizona Game and Fish Department, Arizona State Parks and Trails and California Department of Fish and Wildlife.The trees are collected after the holiday season, bundled with other vegetation and eventually placed in the lake. For the program, the discarded evergreens serve two purposes at once; firstly, they stay out of the landfill and secondly, become temporary underwater structures for fish. The BLM says about 20 regular volunteers help with the work, including bundling and placing the donated materials, and the program also receives brush from local landscapers and collection support from a waste-management service.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: During the Cold War, US aircraft lost nuclear bombs in crashes and decades later, several weapons are still missing beneath the water and mud
articles.summary: US News: Explore the chilling story of three US nuclear bombs lost during the Cold War, their mysterious disappearances, and the challenges of recovering them from underwater depths. Discover where these weapons lie and the efforts to search for them.
articles.body: At least three US nuclear bombs that were lost during the Cold War have never been recovered. One disappeared into waters near Tybee Island, Georgia, in 1958, while another went into the Philippine Sea in 1965 after an aircraft slipped from the USS Ticonderoga. A third was lost after a B-52 crash near Thule Air Base in Greenland in 1968. The weapons remain among the US military's unresolved nuclear-weapon losses. The incidents happened during a period when US aircraft routinely carried nuclear weapons during training and airborne-alert operations. Some weapons were recovered quickly; others disappeared into the sea or were left in locations where recovery proved impossible. The missing weapons were not identical cases since their locations, depths and circumstances differed, and so did the information available about what happened to them.The Tybee bomb disappeared after a forced landingA B-47 bomber that was carrying a Mark 15 thermonuclear bomb was involved in a collision during a training mission near the South Carolina coast on February 5, 1958. The damaged aircraft needed to make an emergency landing. The pilot jettisoned the weapon before landing and dropped it into the waters near Tybee Island, Georgia. Search teams spent almost 10 weeks looking for it before the Air Force declared it irretrievably lost on April 16, 1958.A receipt written by the pilot said that the weapon did not contain its nuclear capsule, while a later Defense Department document described the bomb as complete. BBC Future reported that the weapon is thought to be buried under several feet of silt in Wassaw Sound. In the late 1990s, a retired military officer and his partner searched the area with a Geiger counter after narrowing the likely location to Wassaw Sound. They found a patch with elevated radiation, but the US government determined that the signal came from naturally radioactive minerals rather than the bomb.One weapon is thousands of feet underwaterThe second missing weapon disappeared on December 5, 1965, when an A-4E Skyhawk that was carrying a B43 nuclear bomb rolled toward an aircraft elevator aboard the USS Ticonderoga. The aircraft went over the side of the carrier and disappeared into the Philippine Sea, and the pilot, aircraft and bomb were never recovered. BBC Future reported that the weapon is believed to be lying about 16,000 feet, or roughly 4,900 metres, underwater near a Japanese island.The third case occurred in Greenland in 1968, when a B-52 that was carrying four nuclear weapons caught fire and crashed near Thule Air Base. The crew escaped, but the aircraft and its weapons were destroyed in the crash. The incident produced widespread radioactive contamination from the conventional explosives and nuclear materials in the weapons, although there was no nuclear detonation.The three missing weapons are different from the fourth bomb involved in the 1966 Palomares accident in Spain. That weapon also disappeared underwater, but it was eventually located and recovered after an extensive search using ships, aircraft and the deep-sea submersible Alvin.Finding a nuclear bomb underwater is not like finding a crashed aircraftNuclear weapons did not carry the underwater locator beacons used on aircraft flight recorders, so search teams had to establish probable locations and examine the seabed. Radiation detection was also not a straightforward solution, since nuclear weapons are designed to shield their radioactive material, meaning the detectable radiation signature can be relatively weak at a distance. That leaves investigators dependent on narrowing the search area and conducting visual or physical searches. The Tybee search demonstrated the problem, since even after researchers narrowed the suspected location and detected an unusual radiation signal, the anomaly turned out to be naturally occurring radioactivity in the seabed.The Philippine Sea weapon presents an even greater physical challenge, because a bomb that is sitting almost 16,000 feet below the surface would be far beyond the depth at which ordinary diving operations could work, and would require specialized deep-ocean equipment. BBC Future reported that experts considered it unlikely that the three missing US weapons would ever be found. Their locations are known only within broad areas, and decades underwater or beneath sediment make conventional recovery methods difficult.Catch the latest World News and Live updates.
